title: Add multilingual prompt parity checker CI hook
author: Aisha Rahman
release_notes: Add a CI hook that detects regressions in multilingual prompt parity by comparing normalized outputs across translations; configurable per-language baselines and tolerance thresholds; opt-in via eval-config; no behavioral changes to production runtime; improves detection of translation-induced regressions.
description: Background and motivation: We observed a recurring class of regressions where prompt translations (either human-translated prompt sets or machine back-translated probes) surface quality drops that are not caught by monolingual SLOs. These regressions are subtle because tokenization and punctuation differences can mask semantic drift. This PR introduces a multilingual prompt parity checker as a CI hook to detect regressions that affect parity between language variants of the same prompt set. Design summary: 1) Pair generation: for each canonical prompt set (usually English), the hook pairs it with one or more translated variants (human or machine) and optional back-translated English as a control. 2) Normalization: outputs run through a language-aware normalizer (strip diacritics optionally, unify punctuation, normalize whitespace, unify numbers/dates using locale-aware rules). 3) Metrics: compute semantic-parity score using a symmetric embedding-based similarity (cosine) + token-level fuzzy diff for structural regressions (missing clauses, hallucinated lists). 4) Thresholding and cohorting: per-language baseline means and stddev are stored in the eval registry; checks fail only when the delta exceeds the configured z-score threshold or absolute similarity floor. 5) CI behaviour: the hook runs as an optional evaluation job (eval:multilingual-parity) and can be configured to soft-fail (annotate but not block) or hard-fail depending on linear ticket flags. Implementation notes: - New hook entrypoint eval/hooks/multilingual_parity.py implements pairing, normalization, scoring, and reporting. - A lightweight back-translation adapter lives in eval/adapters/backtranslate_adapter.py used only for generating control pairs in smoke mode. - Baseline storage: eval/registry/multilingual_baselines.csv (small CSV; seeded with en->es,en->fr baseline entries). - Config + opt-in: eval/configs/multilingual_parity.yaml exposes languages, thresholds, and whether to run backtranslate probes. - Tests: unit tests cover normalization edge cases, and an integration smoke test runs on a small curated bilingual prompt set. Backwards compatibility: all changes are behind an opt-in hook; default CI job is gated behind a feature flag so there is zero default test time regression. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag; 2) Enable soft-fail in nightly pipeline for two weeks, collect baseline deviations and false positive counts; 3) Flip to hard-fail for critical products after validation. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of hook logic - [x] Unit tests for normalizer and similarity scorer - [x] Integration smoke test with curated bilingual set - [x] Registry CSV seeded with initial baselines - [x] Docs stub and example config snippet - [x] Linear ticket linked for rollout coordination Testing and results: On the seeded en->es and en->fr sample sets, the semantic-parity metric reproduces existing known-good baselines (mean cosine 0.92 en->es, 0.90 en->fr); the hook triggered one intentional regression injected during development and produced a clear z-score > 4 signal. Observability: the hook emits per-prompt metrics to the eval-metrics namespace (parity.cosine, parity.token_diff_ratio) and summary alerts when > 5% of prompts exceed the configured tolerance. Known limitations: - Back-translation quality depends on the adapter; noisy backtranslations can increase false positives. - Language-specific tokenizers may behave differently between model families; baselines are model-variant-aware but initial CSV is coarse. Documentation: Added README section at docs/eval-hooks/multilingual_parity.md with configuration examples and troubleshooting suggestions.

review_thread: Marco Li: Nice pattern. Two asks: (1) can we make normalization pipeline pluggable so new locales can add rules without changing code? (2) add a short circuit for tiny prompts (<8 tokens) to avoid noisy diffs.
Author (Aisha Rahman): Implemented a NormalizerRegistry that loads rules from eval/configs/normalizers/*.yaml; added token-length short-circuit and updated tests.
Priya Kothari: Can we ensure thresholds are model-variant aware? Suggest adding a model_tag field to baseline CSV.
Author: Added model_tag column to multilingual_baselines.csv and updated parser to match on model_tag when present; falls back to generic baseline when missing.
Jonah Peters: CI time concern: backtranslation added ~20s per prompt for the smoke set. Recommend making backtranslation optional in pipeline and default off in PR runs.
Author: Backtranslation is now opt-in via multilingual_parity.yaml (backtranslate: false by default).
notes: This hook targets a gap in multilingual regression detection and is intentionally opt-in for early rollout; follow-up work ENG-2056 will extend baselines and add model-family calibration.
